papers.title: Sharp Scalar Elliptic Regularity and Certified Degenerate Response
papers.subject: Scalar elliptic equations and homogenization
papers.summary: Sharp estimates describe how scalar elliptic gradients can concentrate, including a local weak endpoint and logarithmic bounds for degenerate media. The paper uses these estimates to certify periodic material response and prove a finite-scale homogenization bound for smooth macroscopic data.
papers.description: Sharp estimates describe how scalar elliptic gradients can concentrate, including a local weak endpoint and logarithmic bounds for degenerate media. The paper uses these estimates to certify periodic material response and prove a finite-scale homogenization bound for smooth macroscopic data.
papers.abstract: We give a scalar-potential extension of the constrained-gradient calibration of Agazzi et al. to real div–curl pairs in every dimension. It yields the exact Lᵖ norm max{p−1, (p−1)⁻¹} of the real-vector Hodge reflection and the sharp open gradient-estimate interval for measurable symmetric scalar elliptic equations, together with the attained sharp local weak endpoint for homogeneous energy solutions and their normalized fluxes. The same calibration, integrated against damped logarithmic weights, proves sharp local regularity under exponentially integrable distortion: if R² ≤ K E·B and exp(τK) is locally integrable, then (E·B) log^β(e+E·B) and (|E|²+|B|²) log^(β−1)(e+|E|+|B|) are locally integrable for every 0 < β < τ. Explicit examples exclude the logarithmic strong endpoint and every general power gain in the degenerate class. We then establish periodic finite-energy solvability, density in the actual anisotropic primal and dual energy spaces, certified rational approximation, and variational homogenization when the coefficient and its inverse have a supplied exponential moment. On a bounded C² domain, smooth macroscopic solutions admit an O(√δ) L² and weighted corrector estimate. A logarithmic modulus also controls effective-response changes under small-region, relatively comparable coefficient edits. The computational theorem uses expanded coefficient data with certified integral error and pays for their acquisition; it is a termination theorem, not a uniform polynomial-time bound. The critical positive div–curl product and the hypercircle principle are identified as prior machinery.

result: An elliptic equation describes a steady balance between a potential and its flux, such as electric potential and current in a conductor. Even when the potential has finite energy, a rough medium can concentrate its gradient strongly. This paper connects sharp bounds on those concentrations with rigorous error certificates for the medium’s effective response.

For bounded symmetric coefficients, the paper identifies the maximal uniform interval of strong gradient estimates and proves the sharp local weak upper endpoint for homogeneous energy solutions. A weak estimate controls how much volume can carry a very large gradient, even when the corresponding power integral diverges. For degenerate media, the separate result gives sharp logarithmic energy bounds under exponentially integrable distortion; explicit examples show why stronger general conclusions fail.

For periodic symmetric media with the stated coefficient and inverse moments, the paper proves finite-energy solvability and exact error certificates for the cell response. It also proves qualitative homogenization, a square-root-scale solution and weighted corrector error bound for smooth macroscopic data, and a logarithmic response-stability bound for small-region edits that remain relatively comparable.
mechanism: The main calibration adapts Agazzi et al.’s scalar constrained-gradient projection: a scalar potential is projected onto potentials whose gradients stay inside a prescribed ball. Pairing the resulting gradient with a divergence-free field supplies a threshold inequality. Power integration gives the reflection bound; retaining the threshold and controlling cutoff errors gives the weak endpoint. Damped logarithmic weights give the degenerate estimates without assuming the integrability being proved.

For periodic response, a positive mean-zero energy pair must vanish. This eliminates the residual of a smooth approximation and proves density in the actual anisotropic energy spaces. The classical primal–dual principle then converts compatible approximate gradients and fluxes into an exact error certificate. The finite-scale proof uses weighted cell and flux potentials, a boundary cutoff and a containing-cube argument that justifies tests in both variational domains.
scope: The equations have a scalar unknown in dimension d ≥ 2; the sharp reflection acts on real vector fields with Euclidean norm. For λI ≤ A ≤ ΛI and s = √(Λ/λ), the strong interval is 2s/(s+1) < p < 2s/(s−1). The finite weak endpoint, when s > 1, is local and homogeneous, with flux normalized as A∇u/√(λΛ). It is not a global forced or arbitrary-boundary endpoint. The uniformly convex homogeneous extension retains D_zW(x,0) = 0.

The degenerate logarithmic estimate requires a locally integrable nonnegative energy product and the stated exponential distortion bound. Periodic response further requires a symmetric positive-definite coefficient and a fixed-unit exponential moment for both coefficient and inverse. The quantitative homogenization result assumes a bounded C² domain and an actual C² zero-trace homogenized solution, with error controlled by its bounded derivatives through order two; its gradient error is weighted by the microscopic coefficient. General-data or optimal rates, stochastic extensions and an unweighted L² gradient bound are not proved.

Small-region response stability requires bounded relative comparability and the actual exponential moments for both media; arbitrary-contrast replacements are not covered. Computation requires supplied expanded coefficient tables with certified integral errors, and charges acquisition, spatial expansion and arithmetic. Finite termination does not imply a uniform polynomial cost or practical solver advantage. Finite point measurements alone do not provide that input representation.

papers.title: Exact Reference-Assisted Entropy Contraction from the Choi Matrix
papers.subject: Quantum information and entropy contraction
papers.summary: An exact finite optimization determines how much distinguishability a quantum channel can preserve in correlations with an untouched memory. The paper connects several entropy measures, separates ordinary mutual-information contraction, and shows why exact channel data and experimental estimation have different limits.
papers.description: An exact finite optimization determines how much distinguishability a quantum channel can preserve in correlations with an untouched memory. The paper connects several entropy measures, separates ordinary mutual-information contraction, and shows why exact channel data and experimental estimation have different limits.
papers.abstract: How much distinguishability can a quantum channel preserve when its input is correlated with an untouched quantum reference? We give an exact finite semidefinite program for the complete, equal-reference Umegaki contraction coefficient of every finite-dimensional channel. Its value also equals the reference-subtracted relative-entropy coefficient and the conditional mutual-information coefficient. The program uses the unnormalized Choi matrix; its inverse formulation requires an explicit range condition. The proof identifies a centered complete Gram optimization, constructs a state-independent signed observable lift through an erasure channel, and proves sharpness with a rare coherent reference sector. References of bounded dimension suffice, even when both input marginals are prescribed and faithful. The same program computes the corresponding coefficients for regular modular Petz divergences, each fixed Petz Rényi order between zero and one, and quantum Chernoff divergence. Consequences include a harmonic dual, exact tensor products, a sharp comparison with positive CP-replacer minorization, and explicit classical and unitary-noise formulas. We separately compute ordinary quantum mutual-information contraction for qubit depolarization, which is strictly smaller. A discontinuity at pure reset rules out uniformly bounded-use black-box estimation, distinguishing exact Choi-data evaluation from robust acquisition of an unknown channel.

result: A noisy quantum channel can erase differences between input states while leaving some information in correlations with a memory outside the channel. This paper asks for the largest fraction of distinguishability that can survive, allowing any finite quantum memory. It compares states with the same memory marginal, or subtracts the distinguishability already present in that memory.

For every finite-dimensional channel, one finite semidefinite program in its Choi matrix gives the exact answer. The complete, reference-subtracted and explicitly conditional-mutual-information coefficients coincide. The same optimization also governs the stated modular Petz divergences, each fixed Petz Rényi order between zero and one, and quantum Chernoff divergence.

Ordinary mutual information allows a quantum reference but has no separate conditioning memory. Its contraction is a different quantity. For a qubit depolarizing channel with shrinkage one half, the ordinary relative-entropy, ordinary mutual-information and complete entropy coefficients are respectively 1/4, 1/3 and 3/8. The paper determines the qubit formulas on the full completely positive parameter interval.
mechanism: The proof first measures how far all output observables are from one common center, retaining their cross terms in a matrix Gram inequality. A Stinespring representation converts this into the Choi optimization. A polar-decomposition argument shows that its center can be chosen positive.

That center gives a signed observable map through an erasure channel. Two separately controlled orders of multiplication produce the universal entropy inequality. For the matching lower bound, a rare coherent memory sector carries a perturbation whose two local marginals vanish exactly. The proof takes the small-perturbation limit first, and only then makes that sector rare.

The matrix formula also yields an exact tensor-product law, a common-output-row criterion for strict contraction and an inverse-probability formula for orthogonal-unitary noise. The ordinary qubit mutual-information calculation uses a separate pinching argument obtained from a classical channel and a flagged unitary orbit.
scope: The input is a finite channel description. The Choi matrix is unnormalized, and the inverse formulation includes an essential support condition even when a pseudoinverse is used. The optimization is finite in Hilbert-space dimension; its matrix size can still be exponential in physical qubit count. No uniformly conditioned or strongly polynomial numerical algorithm is asserted.

The regular modular Petz theorem requires a nonaffine operator-convex generator with finite endpoint value and recession slope. Umegaki entropy has a separate proof. Rényi results concern each fixed order strictly between zero and one, and generalized conditional information means an explicit difference of divergences. They do not cover optimized or sandwiched Rényi conditional information, all orders above one, or a limit uniform in the rare-sector weight.

For higher-dimensional depolarization the ordinary mutual-information coefficient has proved bounds and a strict separation from the complete coefficient, rather than an exact formula. At pure reset the complete coefficient is discontinuous, so no uniformly bounded number of adaptive black-box channel uses estimates it on every channel. Rare sharpness witnesses may carry vanishing absolute information. A signed observable lift is not a physical simulator or a general recovery operation.

papers.title: Spatial Compilation of Stochastic Chemical Trajectories
papers.subject: Stochastic reaction networks and spatial probability
papers.summary: A conservative reversible reaction network can be realized by local elementary reactions among finite-radius particles while approximating its complete timed and labelled trajectory. The construction tolerates specified unknown transport and history-dependent faults, with explicit bounds on dilution, duration, precision and every attempted reaction.
papers.description: A conservative reversible reaction network can be realized by local elementary reactions among finite-radius particles while approximating its complete timed and labelled trajectory. The construction tolerates specified unknown transport and history-dependent faults, with explicit bounds on dilution, duration, precision and every attempted reaction.

result: A well-mixed reaction table describes counts and reaction events without resolving where its particles are. This paper constructs a local finite-radius ideal particle model for conservative reversible targets, with one known clock change and a total-variation bound for the entire timed and labelled reaction record.

The original particles may start at any feasible deterministic placement, including wall and pair contacts, and auxiliary particles start absent. The theorem allows unknown spatially inhomogeneous, time-dependent transport and specified predictable faults that can read the full hidden history.
mechanism: A paired elementary kinetic construction gives intermediate species honest integer payloads and exact nominal activity balance. Anchored forward and reverse placements use matching feasibility indicators; an impossible placement becomes a hidden null attempt rather than a spurious original reaction.

A dilute hard-ball Poincare inequality controls relaxation from arbitrary placements. Its proof separates configurations and compares paths that move one three-dimensional particle coordinate at a time. Conditional proposal coupling then preserves the actual hidden history while comparing complete timed records.
scope: Targets must supply a positive conserved integer weight, a reverse-label involution and rational detailed-balanced activities. This is an ideal finite-radius model in a three-dimensional convex polytope, not a general open-network spatial compiler or a theorem at fixed positive packing density.

Dilution, time and precision costs can be severe. The proved polynomial bound uses a numerical charge including high-order activity, rates, geometry and duration, in addition to binary input length; it does not establish practical affordability.

Real-material implementation, molecular leakage control and thermodynamic energy costs remain unresolved. Nominal spatial balance is exact, but the trajectory guarantee approximates laws and does not identify the decoded equilibrium with an unconditional target Poisson law.

papers.abstract: A well-mixed reaction specification does not by itself determine a local particle implementation. We construct such an implementation for finite labelled mass-action networks with a positive integer conservation law, a supplied reverse involution and prescribed rational detailed-balanced activities. The compiler produces elementary reactions, strictly positive particle radii, constant rational coefficients, a payload decoder and one known slowdown. From every feasible initial placement, including simultaneous contacts, the decoded timed and labelled path approximates the target path in total variation. Transport may be unknown, spatially inhomogeneous and time dependent; the estimate permits full-history predictable chemical, drift and correlated covariance faults within a computed tolerance. A dilute hard-ball Poincaré inequality, proved by buffering, rank separation and one-particle coordinate paths, supplies the required population-uniform polynomial mixing estimates. We account for duration, inverse radii and coefficients, precision, every attempted reaction and the actual wall and pair pushes. The bounds are polynomial in a stated numerical charge together with the binary input length. They allow severe dilution and slowdown and concern an ideal particle model, without asserting a molecular realization or a practical advantage.

companion.description: The kinetic companion supplies the separately proved conservative, detailed-balanced construction in Theorem 9.1. This spatial paper adds finite-radius placement, unknown reflected transport and full trajectory comparison; it does not extend the companion’s general open theorem to space.

papers.title: Compiling Stochastic Chemical Trajectories with Elementary Reactions
papers.subject: Stochastic reaction networks and chemical computation
papers.summary: Finite stochastic mass-action systems with a supplied global drift bound can be compiled into elementary chemistry while approximating their full timed, labelled trajectories. The construction preserves reachability, starts with no auxiliary molecules, and controls errors and costs under coordinated, history-dependent rate perturbations.
papers.description: Finite stochastic mass-action systems with a supplied global drift bound can be compiled into elementary chemistry while approximating their full timed, labelled trajectories. The construction preserves reachability, starts with no auxiliary molecules, and controls errors and costs under coordinated, history-dependent rate perturbations.

result: A stochastic reaction network specifies both what can react and the random timing of its reactions. The main theorem replaces a finite labelled network of variable reaction order by a network with at most two molecules on either side of every reaction, while approximating the law of its entire observed trajectory over a requested finite horizon.

The input must supply a positive integer population weight and a global upper bound on its drift. The compiler preserves directed reachability for every fine state, uses a decoder with no zero columns, and initializes every auxiliary species at exactly zero. Original null and parallel reaction labels remain observable.
mechanism: Private intermediate chains assemble the reactants of each original reaction into a pending species that carries their true decoded population. A completion changes the decoded state by the original reaction, and hidden releases return intermediate payloads to their original species. Small collision-return reactions control work on the actual untruncated run.

A finite-fibre factorial law and an explicit release estimate control the timing error. A marked-path coupling retains exact rescaled event-time coordinates and all original labels. Its auxiliary proposal clocks and equilibrium variables are used only in the proof; the emitted network uses constant rational rates and one known slowdown.
scope: The theorem concerns ideal unit-volume mass-action models, finite-horizon total variation of complete marked-path laws, and sufficiently small predictable multiplicative rate errors on every fine channel. It does not decide the drift promise, provide exact equality of path laws, or control off-graph molecular reactions.

Binary compiler costs are polynomial in the complete expanded input description. Numerical duration, reciprocal rates, tolerance, population and every-event costs are polynomial in a separately stated charge that includes activity at a tail cutoff; this charge may grow rapidly with population and reaction order. No practical affordability or implemented molecular device is established.

A separate theorem constructs a nominally detailed-balanced compiler for reversible targets with prescribed rational activities and a positive conserved integer weight. This is the conservative interface for the spatial companion; neither a general open spatial compiler nor a general open detailed-balanced all-time fault-cost theorem is asserted.

papers.abstract: We construct elementary mass-action networks that approximate the complete labelled trajectories of finite stochastic reaction lists of variable dimension and order. The input supplies a positive integer population weight and a global upper bound on its drift. The compiled structure and decoder depend only on the reaction list; all decoder columns are nonzero, and initialization uses exactly zero auxiliary molecules. Directed reachability is preserved for every fine state. One constant slowdown and rational coefficients give finite-horizon marked-path total-variation accuracy under arbitrary predictable coordinated multiplicative rate errors. Exact rescaled event times, original null labels and parallel labels are retained. A bounded pending-reaction credit and pathwise counting identities pay population and every fine firing throughout the actual untruncated run. Compiler bit costs and charged numerical physical costs have universal polynomial bounds, with reaction order included in the input. A separate paired construction supplies exact nominal detailed balance, conservation and the same timed-path guarantee for conservative reversible inputs with prescribed rational activities. The results concern ideal mass-action models; they do not construct molecular synthesis pathways or establish practical efficiency.

companion.description: The spatial companion realizes the separate conservative, detailed-balanced kinetic theorem using local finite-radius particles and unknown transport. Its geometric and transport argument does not supply a spatial realization for the broader open-network input class of this paper.

papers.title: Programming Nonlinear Magnetic Response with Twelve Mechanical Modes
papers.subject: Magnetohydrodynamics, nonlinear response and ensemble control
papers.summary: A single force in twelve mechanical modes programs a nonlinear velocity and magnetic response to an unknown conserved magnetic mean. The construction works across unknown preparations and time-dependent diffusivities, with explicit error and resource bounds for the full three-dimensional resistive MHD equations.
papers.description: A single force in twelve mechanical modes programs a nonlinear velocity and magnetic response to an unknown conserved magnetic mean. The construction works across unknown preparations and time-dependent diffusivities, with explicit error and resource bounds for the full three-dimensional resistive MHD equations.
papers.abstract: We study prescribed finite-time responses to the unobserved conserved magnetic mean in the three-dimensional viscous, resistive magnetohydrodynamic equations. The control acts only in the momentum equation, through twelve fixed fundamental Fourier shear fields. A deterministic compiler programs an even polynomial velocity response and an odd polynomial magnetic fluctuation of that mean. Its single open-loop force is uniform over a bounded unknown preparation, independent positive spatially constant diffusivity histories with supplied Lipschitz bounds, sufficiently small absolute disturbances, and every energy-admissible weak realization. The degree, coefficient lists and Fourier supports are variable input; physical and binary costs have universal polynomial bounds in the numerical parameters and complete description length. The construction first evaluates odd magnetic registers, loads one collinear packet batch, writes a small even velocity, and amplifies it while preserving the magnetic output. A dyadic return word controls amplification on the whole error space; an inverse-carrier estimate controls the complete unwanted packet output. The result is an endpoint theorem for globally supported periodic forcing. It supplies no hardware, affordability or autonomous computation claim.

result: A conducting fluid carries an unknown conserved magnetic mean: a spatially averaged flux that remains constant during the experiment. This paper asks whether a force chosen in advance can make both final fields depend on that unknown quantity in a prescribed nonlinear way, without measuring it.

The theorem programs an even polynomial velocity response and an odd polynomial magnetic fluctuation, using twelve fixed Fourier shear modes in the momentum equation alone. The polynomial degree and complete rational Fourier coefficient lists are part of the input and satisfy the stated weighted coefficient promise. One force works across the prescribed unknown H¹ preparation class, independent positive spatially constant Lipschitz viscosity and resistivity histories, sufficiently small absolute disturbances, and every admitted energy weak realization.
mechanism: Oscillatory magnetic packets act as registers whose amplitudes hold unknown odd functions of the conserved mean. Mechanical operations route, multiply, restore and decode those amplitudes without measuring them. The construction performs the magnetic arithmetic first, while velocity can still be reset, and assembles one complete collinear packet batch for the final readout.

A single conversion writes a small even velocity response. A mechanical amplifier then enlarges it while returning ideal magnetic transport to the identity. Its stability estimate covers the whole error space, including modes absent from the target. High-frequency clearing, an inverse-carrier bound and explicit error propagation control the unwanted packet output in the actual PDE.
scope: The spatial domain is the periodic unit torus, with globally supported forcing and a prescribed finite final time. The unknown transport coefficients remain positive, spatially constant and Lipschitz in time, with supplied bounds. The preparation, coefficient promise and absolute disturbance tolerance are essential. The theorem does not provide arbitrary path tracking, zero-diffusivity control or fixed relative actuator-error robustness.

The deterministic compiler has universal polynomial bounds in numerical degree, preparation bounds, inverse accuracy, inverse diffusivity, inverse time and temporal regularity, together with complete binary description length. This is not a polynomial-time claim in binary input length alone. Affordable hardware and autonomous computation are not established, and the separate magnetic seed-channel theorem remains conditional on its additional hypotheses.

companion.description: The common-control paper supplies the quantitative reset and finite-mode control foundation. Its endpoint prepares a chosen velocity and erases magnetic fluctuations; the present paper programs a nonlinear response to the unknown conserved magnetic mean.

papers.acknowledgement_note: As stated in the manuscript, additional AI assistance for this paper also included proof development.

papers.title: Twelve-Mode Ensemble Control of Navier–Stokes and Resistive MHD
papers.subject: Fluid equations, magnetohydrodynamics and ensemble control
papers.summary: One prescribed force in twelve spatial modes prepares a chosen velocity and erases magnetic fluctuations across an uncertainty class of three-dimensional conducting fluids. The construction handles unknown time-dependent viscosity and resistivity, with explicit preparation, disturbance and synthesis bounds for finite-time endpoints.
papers.description: One prescribed force in twelve spatial modes prepares a chosen velocity and erases magnetic fluctuations across an uncertainty class of three-dimensional conducting fluids. The construction handles unknown time-dependent viscosity and resistivity, with explicit preparation, disturbance and synthesis bounds for finite-time endpoints.
papers.abstract: We construct a single prescribed momentum force for an uncertainty class of three-dimensional viscous, resistive magnetohydrodynamic equations on the unit torus. The viscosity and magnetic diffusivity are unknown independent Lipschitz functions, with supplied positive lower bounds and a supplied temporal Lipschitz bound. For every unknown initial pair in a joint H¹ ball, the same force prepares a chosen finite Fourier velocity target and returns the magnetic field close to its own unknown conserved mean. The conclusion holds for every admitted additive disturbance and every energy-admissible Leray–Hopf realization. The force uses exactly the twelve fundamental shear fields and ordinary rational time polynomials of degree at most four. A deterministic compiler has fixed polynomial numerical and complete binary resource bounds. The proof combines a concrete returning pressure-driven reset, coupled energy estimates, a full-space nonidentical-cell heat comparison and a depth-two target writer. Navier–Stokes and constant-coefficient cases are specializations. The results concern costly finite-time endpoints with globally supported periodic forcing, not path tracking, zero diffusivity or an economical physical actuator realization.

result: A conducting fluid has two coupled fields: its velocity and its magnetic field. Ensemble control asks for one forcing program that works before the initial fields and transport coefficients are known. Here the uncertainty class is an entire bounded H¹ preparation ball, which controls both the fields and their first spatial derivatives.

The theorem constructs one force in twelve fixed sine and cosine shear fields on the periodic unit torus. At a prescribed final time it prepares a chosen mean-zero, finite Fourier velocity target and brings the magnetic field close to its own conserved spatial mean in the joint L² norm. The same program works for every initial pair and every energy-admissible Leray–Hopf realization in the stated class; it never samples the actual coefficient functions. The Navier–Stokes case follows when the magnetic input and magnetic disturbance vanish.
mechanism: The key reset distinguishes fluid perturbations from magnetic transport. A closed sequence of shears returns particle motion exactly, while the fluid pressure creates a cumulative contraction of velocity perturbations. Signed stirring cells then dissipate magnetic fluctuations, and interleaved resets control the velocity generated by magnetic feedback. The proof pays for fluctuations produced by a constant magnetic input as well as for nonconstant inputs.

After a waiting stage, a finite sequence of shear operations writes the target velocity. The analysis controls coefficient variation over each complete operation without measuring the coefficients. A deterministic compiler turns the program into an ordinary rational force with time polynomials of degree at most four. Coupled energy estimates and strong continuation for the designed horizon transfer the endpoint to every admitted weak realization.
scope: Viscosity and resistivity may be independent unknown real Lipschitz functions, but their positive lower bounds, upper bounds and a common temporal Lipschitz bound must be supplied. The initial pair is real and divergence-free, the velocity has zero mean, and the target is an explicitly supplied rational Fourier polynomial. Disturbances are mean-zero absolute additive errors below the compiler’s tolerance; the theorem does not give fixed fractional actuator or timing robustness. The unknown magnetic mean is conserved.

Force bounds and inverse disturbance tolerance have fixed polynomial bounds in numerical preparation, inverse diffusivity, inverse time, inverse accuracy and temporal regularity parameters. Complete binary work, memory and output costs also include the target description length. This is not a polynomial bound in binary input length alone, and the universal finite precomputation can be extremely large. The theorem concerns costly endpoints under globally supported periodic forcing; arbitrary path tracking, zero diffusivity, economical hardware and a matched engineering advantage are not established.

companion.description: The companion studies a different operation: amplifying a supplied oriented magnetic seed into a known nontrivial field while recovering small total velocity. Its main six-mode construction is independent of the common-control reset; its erasure corollaries use this paper.

papers.acknowledgement_note: As stated in the manuscript, additional AI assistance for this paper also included proof development.

papers.title: Magnetic Seed Amplification with Kinetic Recovery in Resistive Magnetohydrodynamics
papers.subject: Magnetic preparation, fluid control and relative energy
papers.summary: Six mechanical forcing modes amplify a supplied oriented magnetic seed into a known field of fixed nonzero size while recovering small total velocity. The construction controls the coupled three-dimensional resistive MHD equations, with calibrated viscosity, uniform resistivity bounds and explicit preparation and resource costs.
papers.description: Six mechanical forcing modes amplify a supplied oriented magnetic seed into a known field of fixed nonzero size while recovering small total velocity. The construction controls the coupled three-dimensional resistive MHD equations, with calibrated viscosity, uniform resistivity bounds and explicit preparation and resource costs.
papers.abstract: We construct prescribed mechanical forces for the three-dimensional viscous, resistive magnetohydrodynamic equations on a torus. With calibrated viscosity, six fixed mechanical modes take a supplied magnetic seed of size δ and prepare an explicitly represented magnetic field of order one and recover small total velocity. The magnetic L² norm remains bounded throughout. The conclusion holds for every energy-admissible Leray–Hopf realization, uniformly over all positive magnetic diffusivities bounded above, with fixed absolute additive disturbances. A separate construction uses one force for all positive viscosities and diffusivities bounded above and all bounded initial velocities, but guarantees only a magnetic Fourier output. The proofs combine an elementary deterministic selection of ideal shear phases with quantitative relative-energy and duality estimates; numerical synthesis and physical authority have polynomial bounds in the inverse seed and accuracy. We also prove a near-guide-field preparation result with a growing actuator bank. We record common twelve-mode erasure and velocity steering as corollaries of a companion ensemble-control theorem, with constant coefficients and zero magnetic mean. A further joint-target construction with one repeatedly signed magnetic channel remains conditional on explicit smooth-magnetic-prefix implementation estimates. These operations have different preparations and control ports. The results concern costly finite-time endpoints; they do not provide bounded-authority amplification, sustained regulation, or a physical actuator realization.

result: A prescribed fluid motion can stretch a magnetic field, but realizing that motion in a conducting fluid is harder: the magnetic field pushes back on the velocity. This paper constructs an ordinary mechanical forcing program that controls both effects and ends with the total velocity small.

With calibrated viscosity, six fixed forcing modes take a field close to a supplied oriented seed of size δ to an explicitly represented magnetic field of fixed order-one norm. The velocity is recovered near zero, and the magnetic norm stays bounded throughout. One prescribed force works for every positive resistivity in the stated bounded range, every admitted preparation error and absolute disturbance, and every energy-admissible Leray–Hopf realization. The output is chosen by the construction rather than being an arbitrary requested magnetic pattern.
mechanism: The ideal stretching step builds on Rowan’s shear construction. An exact Fourier identity allows three deterministic phase candidates to replace a random phase choice for the known central seed. Repeating the selected steps grows a tracked magnetic observation; an offline stopping rule fixes the final magnetic size. The resulting field has an explicit shear-composition representation that can be evaluated to a requested accuracy.

A rapid forcing program realizes the ideal motion in the coupled equations. Comparing the velocity and magnetic errors together makes their leading nonlinear exchanges cancel, so the proof need not estimate the Lorentz force separately from magnetic energy. Relative-energy bounds then control the physical endpoint, while a finite-bit compiler pays for the force, timing, preparation radius and numerical precision. A weaker magnetic observation uses a backward induction test and tolerates unknown viscosity as well.
scope: The main theorem requires a known oriented central seed, a paid preparation radius around zero velocity and that seed, and calibrated positive viscosity; the force is common over all positive resistivities bounded above by the stated normalization. Its force and synthesis bounds are polynomial in numerical inverse seed size and accuracy, with binary input costs included separately. Seed acquisition and viscosity calibration are not supplied, and absolute error tolerance is not fixed relative actuator accuracy.

The unknown-viscosity theorem guarantees a magnetic observation, without kinetic recovery or full-field accuracy. Near-guide preparation instead uses supplied nonzero flux and a growing actuator bank. Twelve-mode erasure and velocity steering are corollaries of the companion’s endpoint theorem, specialized to constant coefficients and zero magnetic mean. The further joint-target theorem with one signed magnetic channel remains conditional on its separate smooth-prefix implementation hypothesis. These are finite-time operations with large costs; sustained regulation, bounded-authority amplification and a physical actuator realization are not established. Mechanical forcing cannot create magnetism from zero magnetic input.

companion.description: The companion proves a common endpoint theorem for an unknown H¹ preparation ball and unknown time-dependent transport coefficients. It erases fluctuations around the conserved magnetic mean and writes a chosen velocity; this differs from preparing a nontrivial magnetic field from a seed.

papers.title: Global Readouts of Noisy Quantum Dynamics
papers.subject: Open quantum systems, classical simulation and complexity
papers.summary: Independent local noise permits classical prediction of global product readouts in a driven two-dimensional quantum system. The algorithm has polynomial bit complexity at every fixed positive noise ratio, including full-rank biased resets when the Hamiltonian preserves their product reference.
papers.description: Independent local noise permits classical prediction of global product readouts in a driven two-dimensional quantum system. The algorithm has polynomial bit complexity at every fixed positive noise ratio, including full-rank biased resets when the Hamiltonian preserves their product reference.
papers.abstract: We give a randomized polynomial-time classical algorithm for additive prediction of arbitrary products of one-qubit Hermitian contractions in a driven two-dimensional quantum system. Every qubit undergoes replacement at a fixed positive rate. The replacement state may be biased and full rank, provided that the Hamiltonian preserves its product reference; maximally mixed replacement imposes no conservation restriction. The input is a specified product state, the controls have an explicit finite rational description, and the complexity is polynomial in the complete binary input, inverse error and confidence digits, at each fixed positive noise ratio and faithfulness bound. The proof combines coefficient sparsification with a constructible short-time functional: two localized strip states, including retained reset registers, have polynomial Schmidt nuclear norm and admit bounded overlap estimation. Moving coefficient weights and weighted hypercontractivity extend local prediction to readouts of unrestricted support. We also prove a full-output sampler under a supplied bounded-cut certificate, give an acquired-model prediction theorem with explicit uncertainty and preparation costs, and identify two boundaries: rare-probability evaluation remains conditionally hard, and exponentially accurate product means need not determine a distribution in total variation. General intermediate-time two-dimensional output sampling remains open.

result: A product readout combines one local observable from each chosen spin. It can ask about a few spins or about a quantity involving the entire system, such as the parity of all measured bits. Predicting its mean need not require reconstructing the exponentially large quantum state.

This paper gives a randomized classical algorithm for those means in a driven two-dimensional system with independent replacement noise at every site. For a specified product preparation, it achieves any requested additive accuracy in polynomial bit work at each fixed positive noise-to-interaction ratio. Full-rank biased resets are included when the Hamiltonian preserves their product reference; unbiased resets impose no conservation condition.
mechanism: Noise first removes the need to evaluate very late times. For the remaining interval, a moving weight suppresses complicated observable components. Sparse propagation retains a manageable coefficient list, and hypercontractivity describes how the actual early evolution smooths its error enough to control the chosen input.

The early interval must still be computed. The proof expresses its mean as the overlap of two states built on narrow strips. Factorial locality and accumulated interaction strength across a cut keep their tensor dimensions polynomial. A biased reset is represented by swapping in a sampled local state and retaining the discarded register; a concentration bound pays for these extra numerical coordinates. No observation of physical bath records is assumed.
scope: The main theorem requires an explicit finite rational control schedule, bounded interaction range and incidence, and a specified product source. The noise ratio and a positive lower bound on the reset-state eigenvalues are fixed class parameters: the polynomial degree may become very large as noise weakens or the reset state approaches purity. The invariant product reference is generally not the Gibbs state of the interacting Hamiltonian.

A full-output sampler is proved with an additional supplied bounded-cut architecture; generic intermediate-time two-dimensional sampling remains open. The acquired-model application assumes calibrated local preparation and measurement, a known dictionary and noise rate, and pays preparation, precision and model-error budgets. Additive prediction does not provide relative accuracy for rare events, and no implemented general predictor, hardware demonstration or practical advantage is claimed.

papers.title: Quadratic Repetition for Commuting Projection Games and Noisy Quantum Communication
papers.subject: Quantum information, complexity and operator algebras
papers.summary: Repeating a projection game suppresses joint commuting strategies at a quadratic rate in the single-game gap. The paper proves this bound through exact local reconstruction and shows how amplified soundness can survive a precisely charged budget of interactive noisy quantum communication.
papers.description: Repeating a projection game suppresses joint commuting strategies at a quadratic rate in the single-game gap. The paper proves this bound through exact local reconstruction and shows how amplified soundness can survive a precisely charged budget of interactive noisy quantum communication.
papers.abstract: We prove that a finite two-player Boolean game whose supported winning masks are unions of vertex-disjoint complete bipartite blocks satisfies ω_co(Gⁿ) ≤ exp[−2⁻⁷⁵(1 − ω_co(G))²n]. This includes noninjective and partial projection predicates, allows arbitrary within-round question distributions, and holds against arbitrary joint commuting strategies. A separate finite-matrix argument gives the corresponding tensor theorem with its own gap. The quadratic gap power is optimal within the full block class by the known binary line-game lower bound. The main construction gives one exact square-root-weighted conditioned target and two independently normalized one-sided conditional comparisons. Retained-label cancellation, finite-tracial local reconstruction and scalar finite-table closure yield a charged extension and heterogeneous weighted-threshold bounds. We also apply sandwiched-Rényi channel amortization to interactive finite-dimensional protocols: exponential zero-communication soundness survives prescribed memoryless channels below a strict aggregate entanglement-assisted capacity budget. An erasure example has an explicit polynomial-time randomized coding comparator. General quadratic repetition and uniform efficient locality-preserving compilation remain open; no finite-dimensional resource bound is asserted for arbitrary commuting strategies.

result: A nonlocal game asks two separated players to answer correlated questions without communicating. Repeating the game makes the test harder, but the players may coordinate all their answers through one joint quantum strategy. The paper proves that winning every repetition becomes exponentially unlikely for a broad class of projection and block predicates, even for arbitrary commuting-operator strategies.

If the single-game value is 1 − ε, the all-wins probability after n independent rounds is at most exp(−2⁻⁷⁵ε²n). The quadratic power of the gap is optimal within the full block class by known line-game examples. A separate theorem covers finite-dimensional tensor strategies with their own gap.
mechanism: Conditioning on checked wins produces an answer table that need not itself be physically achievable in one round. The proof resolves the winning relation into positive rectangles, records a common label with square-root weights, and compares one exact target to two different one-sided positive states. A private label copy makes an information term cancel exactly.

Conditional relative entropy measures how much information each untested coordinate needs. Local polar corrections and an operational correlated sampler turn small deficits into legal strategies on every input pair. This closes the reconstruction premise left conditional in the earlier entropy-budget paper. Only scalar probability inequalities pass from finite-tracial models to arbitrary commuting correlations.
scope: The quadratic theorem requires each supported winning answer graph to be a union of vertex-disjoint complete bipartite blocks; partial and noninjective projections are included. Question pairs may have any within-round joint distribution, but rounds are independent. General predicates retain a presentation charge, so arbitrary-predicate quadratic repetition remains open.

The noisy-channel extension concerns ordinary finite-dimensional protocols with a question-independent initial resource, or an explicit source-correlation cost. Channel slots are prescribed and memoryless, and every cross-player signal is charged. No uniform finite-dimensional realization of arbitrary commuting strategies, efficient Hamiltonian or cryptographic compiler, historical priority, or implemented physical advantage is claimed.

papers.title: Quantum Memory from Rare Thermal Boundaries
papers.subject: Quantum information and mathematical physics
papers.summary: A thermally rare error boundary can protect an unknown quantum state under exact system–bath dynamics. The paper proves storage bounds proportional to the boundary probability and holding time, and identifies the preparation and access assumptions needed to turn equilibrium estimates into a memory guarantee.
papers.description: A thermally rare error boundary can protect an unknown quantum state under exact system–bath dynamics. The paper proves storage bounds proportional to the boundary probability and holding time, and identifies the preparation and access assumptions needed to turn equilibrium estimates into a memory guarantee.
papers.abstract: A logical observable can change slowly because its commutator with the Hamiltonian is supported on a thermally rare subspace. Turning this observation into a memory theorem requires control of the state after an unknown input has been written. We give two complete criteria for that step under the exact joint system–bath dynamics. If all three logical Pauli commutators are supported on a common projection of Gibbs probability p, with summed norm bound a, ideal subsystem replacement gives deterministic half-diamond error at most ap|t|F(βa/4), where F(K) = inf over λ > 0 of (K + exp(λ) − 1)/λ. A Pauli-randomized protocol instead has error at most ap(2|t| + β)/4. The proofs use rare-event relative entropy and a Bell-projection identity, respectively. The latter identity also gives a dimension-independent correlation criterion for arbitrary correlated resources and arbitrary joint quantum channels, including an algebraic infinite-bath formulation. We identify precise sufficient conditions for imperfect writing and prove that global domination by a thermal encoder can fail exponentially even for harmless independent gauge faults. All storage statements assume a specified accessible logical algebra and a fixed joint resource; preparation cost and a generic noisy-writing threshold are not supplied. The results are abstract criteria, rather than a new three-dimensional memory construction.

result: A quantum memory must preserve an unknown state, including its entanglement with another system. Thermal equilibrium can help when the configurations that allow a logical error are extremely rare. This paper gives precise conditions under which that equilibrium rarity protects a newly written input under the actual joint dynamics of the memory and its environment.

If the logical observables change only on a boundary of equilibrium probability p, the storage error is bounded by an explicit constant times p times the holding time. An exponentially rare boundary therefore gives a correspondingly long conditional storage interval. A two-qubit example shows the mechanism and explains why the bound is sufficient rather than an optimal lifetime for every model.
mechanism: Writing swaps the external input into an accessible logical subsystem while retaining the original joint marginal of all remaining variables and the bath. The relative-entropy cost of this replacement is proportional to the rare-boundary probability. Measuring only that boundary event, rather than estimating the entire state in trace distance, keeps the full rarity factor through the proof.

A second argument uses a Bell-state test to convert a complete set of logical correlations into a bound on the memory channel. Randomizing the input Pauli and undoing it after reading gives a guarantee valid even for entangled inputs. This protocol requires two reliably retained classical frame bits. The general channel criterion also works for arbitrary correlated resources and joint quantum channels.
scope: The thermal theorem assumes an exact accessible logical qubit algebra on the whole physical Hilbert space, two-sided support of all three logical commutators on a common projection, and the actual interacting Gibbs resource. The equilibrium rare-event estimate must be established separately for the model. Neither locality nor an efficient implementation of the logical swap follows from the abstract theorem.

The paper does not construct a new three-dimensional code, prepare an interacting Gibbs state efficiently, or prove a threshold for realistic noisy writing. Its imperfect-writing theorems are sufficient interfaces; counterexamples show why an accurate logical marginal at release is not enough. The infinite-bath extension applies to the general channel criterion and its stated invariant-state consequence, and the collective-symmetry application retains its separate exact symmetry and energy-scale assumptions.

papers.title: Greatest Quantum Channels with Prescribed Maximal Information
papers.subject: Quantum information and operator algebras
papers.summary: Quantum channels can share every complete maximal-information test while differing in what they can physically simulate. The paper constructs their greatest finite realizations and shows how atomicity and injectivity govern exact and approximate realizations for infinite outputs with a tracial invariant.
papers.description: Quantum channels can share every complete maximal-information test while differing in what they can physically simulate. The paper constructs their greatest finite realizations and shows how atomicity and injectivity govern exact and approximate realizations for infinite outputs with a tracial invariant.
papers.abstract: Equality of quantum information measures need not imply recoverability. We study the class of all channels having the same right logarithmic derivative Fisher information for every faithful input, tangent, and finite reference system. These data determine a generated von Neumann algebra, its labelled normalized channel, and a faithful normal state. For finite outputs this invariant yields a greatest channel under deterministic postprocessing, of minimum possible output dimension. For separable trace-class outputs and a tracial invariant state, a greatest member exists exactly when the invariant is a countable product of finite matrix algebras. Arbitrarily accurate greatest members inside the same exact profile class exist exactly when the invariant is injective. In the latter statement a common sequence approximating each fixed target already implies the existence of a uniformly approximating sequence. The proofs combine physical resolvent tests, spectral pinching, finite-dimensional averaging, and established operator-algebraic approximation theory. We give an explicit free-group obstruction, polynomial-bit separating tests for rational finite channels, and a fixed full-support family for which the optimized capacity of the profile class is discontinuous although every physical channel is antidegradable. The atomic/injective distinction and the underlying sufficiency and amenability machinery are established; the formulation here fixes the complete information profile and requires its optimizing sources to remain in that class.

result: Two quantum channels can agree on a large family of information measures without having the same physical capabilities. This paper fixes their complete right logarithmic derivative (RLD) information profile: it requires equality for every faithful input state, every infinitesimal change of that state and every finite quantum reference system left untouched by the channel.

A greatest realization is one channel from which every other channel with that exact profile can be produced by ordinary deterministic postprocessing. For a finite-dimensional invariant algebra, the paper constructs such a realization using the smallest possible effective output dimension. Among separable density-operator outputs with a faithful tracial invariant state, exact greatestness is equivalent to a countable product of finite matrix blocks. Uniformly accurate greatest realizations within the same exact class exist precisely when the invariant algebra is injective.

A simple example explains why this question is different from ordinary recoverability. Orthogonal classical records and certain nonorthogonal pure-state records have identical complete RLD profiles. The orthogonal records can prepare the nonorthogonal ones, but no channel can turn the latter back into perfectly distinguishable records.
mechanism: The first step normalizes each output by the channel’s output on the identity. The normalized operators generate an algebra, and the output density gives it a weighted state. A finite reference arranged as a path turns an ordered product of normalized operators into a coefficient of a resolvent. Four elementary reference projectors read its real and imaginary parts. All complete physical tests therefore determine the labelled algebra and state.

Finite matrix blocks can be represented once each, with explicit trace-preserving preparation maps to every other realization. In the infinite tracial setting, spectral pinching constructs fixed targets that attain the largest possible binary testing norm. Simulating those targets forces source densities toward centrality. Conversely, averaging a density over finite-dimensional unitary groups preserves its entire exact profile and yields uniform approximation. The operator-algebraic classification and amenability machinery used at this step are established results and are credited in the paper.
scope: The input dimension is finite. Infinite outputs are ordinary trace-class density operators on separable Hilbert spaces, and physical postprocessings have normal adjoints. The infinite exact and approximate classification requires a faithful normal tracial invariant state; the finite-dimensional greatest-representative theorem does not. The infinite nontracial problem remains open.

The approximation theorem requires a single source sequence that works for every fixed target in the class. It proves that existence of such a sequence is equivalent to existence of a sequence with uniform diamond-norm error over all targets. The sources themselves retain the exact original profile, but their outputs may remain infinite dimensional. No computable general filtration or convergence rate is supplied.

For explicit rational finite channels, exact profile equality and faithful separating witnesses have polynomial description cost; the information gap may nevertheless be exponentially small. A fixed full-support family shows that capacity optimized over an exact profile class can jump even though every physical channel in the family has zero quantum capacity. This is consistent with continuity of ordinary channel capacity. Complete RLD-profile equality is a different problem from complete SLD, Umegaki and Holevo information order.

papers.title: Entropy Budgets and Weighted Concentration in Parallel Games
papers.subject: Probability and quantum information
papers.summary: An explicit conditional entropy budget forces weighted concentration even when test outcomes are arbitrarily correlated. The paper also identifies barriers to positive-factor reconstruction; applications to commuting-operator games retain a separately stated reconstruction hypothesis.
papers.description: An explicit conditional entropy budget forces weighted concentration even when test outcomes are arbitrarily correlated. The paper also identifies barriers to positive-factor reconstruction; applications to commuting-operator games retain a separately stated reconstruction hypothesis.
papers.abstract: We prove a concentration principle for arbitrarily correlated binary success indicators satisfying an explicit conditional entropy budget, with parameters K ≥ 1 and C₀ ≥ 0. If the benchmark losses are εᵢ, the natural scale is S = ∑ᵢ εᵢ², and the probability that the weighted loss ∑ᵢ εᵢ(1 − Wᵢ) is at most (1 − r)S is bounded by exp[−r⁵S/(2²¹K⁴(1 + C₀))]. The proof uses independent sparse success tests, an exact posterior entropy identity and a differential bound, and applies at every finite length. Under a separately stated finite-tracial reconstruction hypothesis, the principle gives heterogeneous commuting-game bounds for disjoint-block predicates, including projection predicates, and a charged extension. We also identify the exact limitation of positive-factor mass bounds: outside the disjoint-block class, global tensor factorizations can require exponential mass even at success probability one. A robust common-information argument rules out uniformly low-mass accurate filters on all near-perfect tested instances. Nevertheless independent question-free nuisance registers cancel exactly from entropy increments. This separates an obstruction to positive-mass reconstruction from the unresolved problem of controlling entropy directly for general correlated strategies.

result: When many tests are performed together, dependence between their outcomes can defeat the usual concentration arguments. This paper gives a sufficient conditional entropy budget that controls how much the untested coordinates can improve after selected successes have been revealed.

Under that budget, the chance of an unusually small weighted loss decreases exponentially in the sum of the squared benchmark losses. The theorem allows different losses at different coordinates and holds at every finite length. A sharper estimate covers the event that every test succeeds.
mechanism: The proof introduces independent sparse auxiliary tests and conditions on their success. Only these auxiliary choices are independent: the actual outcomes may be arbitrarily correlated. An exact identity tracks the entropy cost of this conditioning, and a differential bound converts that cost into concentration.

A separate part of the paper examines attempts to reconstruct strategies using positive factorizations of the acceptance rule. It identifies the exact disjoint-block class with the required mass control, proves exponential obstructions outside that class, and shows why independent question-free nuisance registers can still cancel from entropy increments even when endpoint masses grow.
scope: The concentration theorem assumes the displayed conditional entropy budget. Its commuting-operator game applications assume Hypothesis FR(K), a finite-tracial coordinate reconstruction property that is not proved here. At its purely existential level, FR(K) is equivalent to the corresponding finite-tracial scalar budget. Projection predicates are included under this hypothesis.

The robust obstruction to uniformly low-mass accurate filters concerns all near-perfect tested instances at bounded universal charge with growing answer alphabets. It limits this reconstruction method and does not disprove general quadratic parallel repetition. Exact nuisance cancellation requires a literal product state, product measurements and a product conditioning event.

General correlated-nuisance subtraction, unconditional quadratic repetition for arbitrary predicates and optimal threshold rates remain open. Established quadratic bounds for unique games are credited separately.
