papers.title: Finite Certificates and Undecidable Gibbs Uniqueness
papers.subject: Mathematical physics
papers.summary: At one fixed positive temperature, a family of classical spin models encodes whether a computation ever halts. Uniqueness is undecidable within this family, yet each model on its unique-equilibrium branch has exponentially decaying correlations.
papers.abstract: We construct translation-invariant classical interactions on ℤ² for which deciding uniqueness among all Gibbs states is undecidable at inverse temperature one. The finite on-site alphabet depends effectively on the input; interaction supports are fixed, and local energy terms take only the integer values 0, 1, 20. Exact character orthogonality converts a strictly positive finite-energy model into a gas of finite computation histories. A halting certificate produces a uniformly positive phase-selection bias, however small. A reference Ising comparison and an independent-disagreement argument then give uniqueness and exponential clustering of every local physical observable. Without halting, the entire Gibbs simplex is affinely isomorphic to the two-dimensional zero-field Ising simplex. A distinct soft-certificate construction has the same dichotomy for one table at every finite inverse temperature at least 2/5. We prove boundary-specific exponential convergence, smooth pressure with summable cumulants on the uniqueness branch, uniform computability of the selected phase and its right pressure jet, and stability under small finite-range spin perturbations. An effective compactness argument supplies a computable valid convergence modulus for each unique computable finite-range specification; the impossibility concerns total bounds across the undecidable family. Exact microscopic symmetrization excludes a family-wide perturbation radius for arbitrary real interactions.
papers.description: At one fixed positive temperature, a family of classical spin models encodes whether a computation ever halts. Uniqueness is undecidable within this family, yet each model on its unique-equilibrium branch has exponentially decaying correlations.

result: The paper constructs finite-range classical models on the square lattice whose equilibrium phases encode whether a computation halts. If it halts, there is exactly one Gibbs state, and correlations of all bounded local physical observables decay exponentially. If it never halts, the full set of Gibbs states is an affine copy of the low-temperature, zero-field two-dimensional Ising simplex.

This separates two questions that can look similar: how correlations behave inside an equilibrium state, and whether an algorithm can decide that the state is the only equilibrium. The undecidability concerns uniqueness among all Gibbs states, including states that are not translation invariant.
mechanism: A halting computation has a finite accepting history. Finite-group character identities make invalid histories cancel exactly in an expansion of the partition function, even though every physical Boltzmann weight is strictly positive. A valid history produces a positive phase-selection bias, however small.

An Ising comparison and independent disagreement coverings then control the remaining fluctuations. Replica swaps transfer the resulting decay estimate to every local physical observable, including the auxiliary variables used to encode the computation.
scope: The main construction fixes inverse temperature β = 1, uses fixed interaction supports and local energy values 0, 1 and 20, and allows the finite on-site alphabet to vary effectively with the computation. A separate soft-certificate construction uses one interaction table at every finite β ≥ 2/5.

Finite-volume rates apply to the boundary conventions specified in the paper. Infinite-volume clustering does not supply arbitrary-boundary strong spatial mixing. Pressure smoothness and perturbation stability retain their stated hypotheses.
Each unique computable finite-range specification has a computable valid convergence modulus. The obstruction concerns total bounds across the undecidable family.

papers.title: Fixed-format undecidability of exact catalytic tensor restriction
papers.subject: Quantum information and algebraic complexity
papers.status: AI-generated proof candidate; independent validation and priority review pending
papers.summary: A catalyst can enable an exact quantum-state conversion while being returned unchanged. A proposed tensor construction connects this effect to algebra representations and an undecidable conversion problem within one fixed positive tensor family.
papers.abstract: A proposed representation compiler links finite-dimensional representations of finitely presented rational associative algebras to exact stochastic restriction of three-tensors with an exactly returned bipartite maximally entangled catalyst. Rank-drop markers constrain otherwise unrestricted local maps. The resulting construction gives a route to recursively enumerable complete conversion along a fixed rank-one affine family of strictly positive integer tensors, together with a finite example of genuine catalysis. The model concerns exact conversion with unbounded catalyst dimension; it imposes no uniform positive success probability.
papers.rights_notice: No additional licence is granted by this website.
papers.description: A catalyst can enable an exact quantum-state conversion while being returned unchanged. A proposed tensor construction connects this effect to algebra representations and an undecidable conversion problem within one fixed positive tensor family.

result: The manuscript proposes a compiler from finitely presented rational associative algebras to three-party tensors. At each positive integer d, conversion with an exactly returned rank-d bipartite catalyst is equivalent to the existence of a unital d-dimensional complex matrix representation of the algebra.

The proposed reduction places an undecidable conversion problem along a single fixed rank-one affine family of strictly positive integer tensors. A small algebra with two anticommuting involutions supplies a concrete example: a two-dimensional representation exists although no scalar representation does, giving a proposed witness of genuine catalysis.
mechanism: The challenge is to force arbitrary local tensor maps to respect the algebraic equations encoded in their matrix slices. The construction adds labelled blocks whose ranks drop on prescribed hyperplanes. These rank patterns are intended to pin down slice mixing, while a full-rank marker prevents auxiliary coordinates from concealing an invalid representation.

A representation-theoretic integer encoding and a universal Diophantine equation then transfer a computation problem into one varying tensor coefficient. A fixed invertible change of basis makes the tensors strictly positive.
scope: The model is exact stochastic tensor restriction over the complex numbers. The catalyst is bipartite, its dimension is unbounded, and it is returned exactly and uncorrelated with the target on the successful branch. Success probability has no uniform positive lower bound.

The representation compiler and its consequences are presented as a proposed construction. Approximate return, deterministic local operations and a fixed positive success-rate guarantee require separate results.

papers.title: Thermal balance and the amplifier entropy photon-number inequality
papers.contribution: Harjas Sandhu developed and coordinated the agentic system used for this investigation. The mathematical development and writing are AI-generated; no human mathematical authorship is assigned.
papers.subject: Quantum information and mathematical physics
papers.rights_notice: The source bundle retains the Apache License 2.0 and attribution notice for incorporated OpenAI material. See LICENSE and NOTICE.txt for scope.
papers.abstract: The entropy photon number is the occupation of a thermal state with a given entropy per mode. We give a variational argument for its sharp lower bound under amplification of two independent finite-energy inputs, allowing correlations within each input group. The proof turns on an agreement of signs: the creation port reverses a logarithmic-mean metric, and thermal relaxation obeys the corresponding signed occupation balance. At a regularized entropy minimum, these two facts cancel the energy corrections and force the thermal-balance defects to vanish. A trace-norm Stein bound, obtained from thermal-attenuator smoothing, then closes the argument. We also give a Gaussian spectral refinement, characterize Gaussian equality by a common symplectic shape, and deduce a sharp correlation bound for the two outputs. The conjecture is due to De Palma, Mari and Giovannetti; the variational framework and four-weight interpolation are adapted from OpenAI's beam-splitter argument.
papers.provenance: This manuscript emerged from an iterative, substantially autonomous research process involving several AI systems, with successive rounds of dialogue, mathematical investigation, criticism and rewriting coordinated through human direction. The mathematical development and writing are AI-generated; established contributions are credited in the text.
papers.provenance_summary: The variational framework and four-weight interpolation adapt OpenAI’s beam-splitter argument. The amplifier conjecture is credited to De Palma, Mari and Giovannetti. The inherited license and attribution notice are included with the complete source.
papers.verification_status: The general amplifier argument is a proof candidate. The release has passed file-integrity, source-structure, compilation and presentation checks. These checks do not establish independent specialist review, formal proof verification or priority for the refinements.
papers.summary: Quantum amplification adds unavoidable noise. A variational argument seeks the sharp lower bound on output entropy for two independent inputs, even when the modes within either input are correlated.
papers.description: Quantum amplification adds unavoidable noise. A variational argument seeks the sharp lower bound on output entropy for two independent inputs, even when the modes within either input are correlated.

result: The entropy photon number expresses a state’s entropy as the occupation of a thermal state with the same entropy per mode. The manuscript presents a variational argument for its sharp amplifier lower bound: at gain G, the output entropy photon number is at least G times the first input’s value plus (G − 1) times the sum of the second input’s value and one.

Thermal inputs attain the bound. For example, gain 2 and thermal occupations 1 and 0 give output occupation 3. The proposed inequality says that independent inputs with those same entropies cannot produce a smaller output entropy photon number.
mechanism: The amplifier’s second input enters through a creation operator. That reversal changes the sign structure of a logarithmic-mean comparison and introduces the extra quantum-noise term. Thermal relaxation obeys a matching signed balance.

At a regularized entropy minimum, the two structures cancel the energy corrections. A thermal Stein estimate is then used to turn small balance defects into trace-norm closeness to thermal states, with finite-energy estimates closing the proposed argument. The variational framework and four-weight interpolation build on the earlier beam-splitter argument.
scope: The general argument concerns two independent finite-energy input groups with any fixed finite number of modes. Correlations and entanglement within either group are allowed. Correlations between the two groups can violate the independent-input formula.

The manuscript also studies Gaussian spectral refinements and Gaussian equality. General non-Gaussian equality and a quantitative stability theorem remain open. The proposed general amplifier argument and its Gaussian special cases should be read at their respective scopes.

papers.title: An example of a non-sofic hyperbolic group
papers.subject: Group theory
papers.abstract: We construct a torsion-free, two-dimensional, word-hyperbolic group which is not sofic. Our construction builds on OpenAI's construction of a non-residually finite hyperbolic group, see OpenAI 252.
papers.provenance: This paper is based on an AI-generated construction obtained by Harjas Sandhu on October 7, 2026, which was in turn based on the OpenAI breakthrough [14]. The second author worked through the proof to make it readable and to reduce unnecessary overhead.
papers.provenance_summary: The construction inherits marked lines, triangular relations, an interpolation identity and comparisons of real and finite-field ranks from OpenAI 252. The acknowledgments also disclose AI assistance in drafting and explain how the paper relates these ingredients to earlier mathematics. The PDF hosted here is the unchanged arXiv v1 preprint.
papers.summary: A negatively curved group can resist approximation by finite permutations. The paper constructs a torsion-free, two-dimensional hyperbolic group that is not sofic, linking geometric group theory with the limits of finite models.
papers.description: A negatively curved group can resist approximation by finite permutations. The paper constructs a torsion-free, two-dimensional hyperbolic group that is not sofic, linking geometric group theory with the limits of finite models.
papers.acknowledgement_note: For this coauthored paper, the AI acknowledgement describes the initial construction stage. Andreas Thom subsequently worked through the proof and revised its exposition, as recorded in the published acknowledgements.

result: A group is sofic when every finite part of its multiplication law can be modelled, to arbitrarily small error, by permutations of a finite set. The paper constructs a torsion-free word-hyperbolic group for which such approximations fail.

The group is the fundamental group of a finite two-dimensional triangle complex with a locally CAT(−1) metric. Its geometric description and obstruction to finite permutation models hold simultaneously, providing an explicit connection between negative curvature and failure of sofic approximation.
mechanism: The construction uses marked lines in a finite incidence geometry to prescribe triangular relations. Polynomial interpolation and matrix-rank estimates force a uniform obstruction: any permutation assignment either violates a triangle relation on a positive fraction of points or makes a designated four-edge word fix too many points.

A large-girth incidence graph supports the negative-curvature metric and ensures that the designated words are nontrivial. These two alternatives are incompatible with arbitrarily accurate sofic approximations. The construction builds on the earlier non-residually finite hyperbolic-group construction credited in the paper.
scope: The approximation notion is soficity: approximate multiplication and separation in finite symmetric groups, measured by normalized Hamming distance. Ruling out exact finite quotients alone would not establish this obstruction.

The theorem produces a specific finite presentation and a finite connected triangle complex. The geometric conclusion is torsion-free word hyperbolicity; the construction does not aim to minimize the presentation size.

papers.title: Complete information orders of quantum channels: equivalence and undecidability
papers.contribution: Harjas Sandhu developed and coordinated the agentic system used for these investigations and serves as the manuscript contact, rather than as a scientific author.
papers.subject: Quantum information

companion.description: The companion preprint develops capacity and one-way distillation consequences that depend on the order results presented here.

papers.abstract: With arbitrary finite quantum references, relative entropy, Holevo information and SLD Fisher information induce the same channel order, reversed by complementation. This order is coRE-complete, even for strictly positive rational POVMs. Its bounded entropy defect is additive and uncomputable at every fixed positive additive accuracy.
papers.provenance: The new results and proofs were discovered and developed by AI systems. Harjas Sandhu serves solely as the contact person. Independent specialist review and priority assessment are pending.
papers.summary: Several ways to ask whether one quantum channel preserves more information turn out to give the same answer when every finite quantum reference is allowed. That complete comparison remains undecidable, even for strictly positive rational measurements.
papers.description: Several ways to ask whether one quantum channel preserves more information turn out to give the same answer when every finite quantum reference is allowed. That complete comparison remains undecidable, even for strictly positive rational measurements.

result: Quantum channels can be compared by their preservation of relative entropy, Holevo information or symmetric logarithmic derivative Fisher information. Allowing an arbitrary finite untouched quantum reference makes these three comparisons equivalent. Passing to complementary channels reverses the order.

The resulting comparison problem is coRE-complete, already for measurements with strictly positive rational-complex effects. The paper also gives an additive bounded entropy defect whose value cannot be computed to any fixed positive rational additive accuracy.
mechanism: An untouched reference is an auxiliary quantum system that may be correlated with the input. Its freedom connects local Fisher-information tests to global entropy comparisons through coherent blocks and resolvent identities. A purification identity relates information retained by the receiver to information lost to the environment.

For the undecidability reduction, finite nonlocal games are encoded into inverse Sylvester kernels and then into strictly positive measurement effects. Finite witnesses detect failed comparisons, but their required reference dimensions have no computable uniform bound.
scope: Each individual channel, measurement and test is finite dimensional. Completeness quantifies over every finite reference dimension, with no common bound. The equivalence is a statistical information order; it does not by itself assert that one channel can be obtained by physically processing the other.
The fixed-accuracy obstruction concerns the bounded entropy defect defined in the paper. Its conclusion depends on the complete comparison and the specified exact input representation.

papers.title: From complete channel order to capacity and one-way distillation
papers.contribution: Harjas Sandhu developed and coordinated the agentic system used for these investigations and serves as the manuscript contact, rather than as a scientific author.
papers.subject: Quantum information

companion.description: This manuscript develops capacity and distillation consequences using the complete-order results of the companion preprint.

papers.abstract: A flagged channel with a four-dimensional auxiliary input turns every failed complete information comparison into positive private and quantum capacity. This transfers complete-order undecidability to exact-zero capacity and one-way distillation, even under any prescribed two-way distillation lower bound. All reference transmission and activation use the constructed channel itself.
papers.provenance: The new results and proofs were discovered and developed by AI systems. Harjas Sandhu serves solely as the contact person. Independent specialist review and priority assessment are pending.
papers.summary: An information advantage can be converted into a positive communication rate using the constructed channel itself. The reduction makes exact-zero quantum and private capacity, and related one-way distillation questions, undecidable.
papers.description: An information advantage can be converted into a positive communication rate using the constructed channel itself. The reduction makes exact-zero quantum and private capacity, and related one-way distillation questions, undecidable.

result: The paper turns a pair of quantum channels into one flagged channel with a four-dimensional auxiliary input. Complete information dominance holds exactly when the constructed channel has zero private capacity, and exactly when it has zero quantum capacity.

A failed comparison therefore produces a positive communication rate. The construction transfers the companion paper’s undecidability to exact-zero capacity and to one-way entanglement and key distillation, even with a prescribed positive lower bound on two-way distillation.
mechanism: The comparison witness may involve a large quantum reference, which communication does not supply for free. Repeated uses of the flagged channel distribute that reference in quantum shares together with a classical key. The routing and key structure make unsuccessful patterns harmless and retain a finite positive private-information witness.

Further uses of the same channel realize the helper needed to convert this private advantage into positive coherent information. All transmission and activation resources are provided by the constructed channel; no separate reference channel is assumed.
scope: The capacities are the ordinary unassisted quantum and private classical capacities of a finite-dimensional memoryless channel. The witnessing reference dimension, blocklength and positive rate may depend on the input channel pair.

The undecidability distinguishes exactly zero from strictly positive capacity. It supplies no uniform positive rate gap and does not by itself obstruct additive approximation of capacity. The distillation consequences use the constructions and hypotheses stated in the paper.

research_intro.heading: Mathematical foundations for new capabilities

I hope these results can be examined, connected and built on by researchers and engineers, leading to new theories, methods and applications.

papers.note: One twelve-mode force prepares a chosen velocity and erases magnetic fluctuations across the stated uncertainty class.

papers.label: Nonlinear response
papers.note: Uses the quantitative common-control foundation to program a joint polynomial response to the unknown conserved magnetic mean.

papers.label: Magnetic preparation
papers.note: Amplifies a supplied oriented seed while recovering small velocity. Its direct preparation construction has a different input contract.

research_connections.title: Prediction and protection under quantum noise
research_connections.description: Three complementary questions: what can be predicted, what can be retained, and how noise constrains output entropy. Each paper uses its own physical model and assumptions.

papers.label: Predicting readouts
papers.note: Local noise permits classical prediction of specified global observations in driven two-dimensional quantum systems.

papers.label: Protecting information
papers.note: Storage bounds use thermally rare error boundaries and explicit preparation and access assumptions.

papers.label: Entropy of amplification
papers.note: A proposed variational argument addresses output entropy for quantum amplifiers; Gaussian results retain their separate scope.

research_connections.title: Comparing quantum information
research_connections.description: These papers distinguish statistical channel orders, exact entropy-loss coefficients and physical simulation. Capacity consequences use the channel-order construction; maximal-information profiles concern a different invariant.

papers.label: Complete information order
papers.note: Relates information comparisons with arbitrary finite references and establishes undecidability at the stated exact scope.

papers.label: Communication consequences
papers.note: Uses the companion order results to derive exact-zero capacity and one-way distillation obstructions.

papers.label: Maximal-information profiles
papers.note: Studies RLD profiles and canonical realizations. Equality of these profiles is distinct from the complete order used in the companion pair.

papers.label: Exact entropy contraction
papers.note: Computes complete and conditional information-loss coefficients from one finite channel's Choi matrix, and separates them from ordinary mutual-information contraction.

research_connections.title: Amplifying tests through repetition
research_connections.description: Entropy accounting controls correlated test outcomes. Applying it to a game also requires a reconstruction argument; the projection-game paper supplies a result for its specified predicate class.

papers.label: Entropy and concentration
papers.note: Develops weighted concentration and identifies reconstruction barriers; its commuting-game applications retain a reconstruction hypothesis.

papers.label: Projection games and communication
papers.note: Proves quadratic repetition for commuting projection games and charges a specified budget of noisy quantum communication.

research_connections.title: Limits of computation and finite description
research_connections.description: These papers examine different uses and limits of finite mathematical descriptions: equilibrium uniqueness, certified elliptic response, finite group models and exact catalytic conversion. Their questions are connected thematically; they do not share one construction.

papers.label: Equilibrium uniqueness
papers.note: A fixed-temperature spin family encodes halting, while its unique-equilibrium branch has exponentially decaying correlations.

papers.label: Certified elliptic response
papers.note: Constructs response certificates from supplied integral approximations and separates finite termination from uniform computational cost.

papers.label: Finite group models
papers.note: Constructs a hyperbolic group that cannot be approximated by finite permutations in the sense of soficity.

papers.label: Catalytic conversion
papers.note: A proposed representation compiler links exact tensor restriction with an undecidable conversion problem. Its construction status is retained.
